2027-05-08.title: Saturday of the Sixth Week of Easter
readings: Apollos showed by the scriptures that the Messiah is Jesus
God is king of all the earth (or: Alleluia)
The Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed
2027-05-08.alt: Easter weekday. The paschal candle burns beside the ambo; the Alleluia is sung before the Gospel; the Regina Caeli (Queen of Heaven) replaces the Angelus until Pentecost. Liturgical colour: white. Saturday, a day traditionally dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary. In India the Ascension is celebrated tomorrow; this evening's Mass is the Vigil Mass of the Ascension. Second day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-08.verse: For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
theo: Today's short reading opens Paul's third great journey. After a visit to Antioch, his home church, “he departed and went from place to place through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.” Luke gives only one line to hundreds of kilometres on foot, but the purpose is clear: a missionary does not only found churches; he goes back to strengthen them. Then the scene moves to Ephesus, where Priscilla and Aquila have settled, and a new figure appears: Apollos, a Jew from Alexandria in Egypt, the great city of books and scholars. Luke paints him warmly: “an eloquent man, well-versed in the scriptures,” instructed in the Way of the Lord, speaking “with burning enthusiasm” and teaching “accurately the things concerning Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.” He had a gift, a fire, and a gap.

What happens next is a quiet model of Christian correction. “When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately.” They do not interrupt him in the synagogue or denounce him to the apostles. They take him aside, probably into their home and workshop, and teach him. A tentmaking couple instruct a brilliant preacher, and he is humble enough to learn. Notice too that Luke again names Priscilla first: a woman and her husband together hand on the faith. Then the believers write a letter of recommendation, Apollos crosses to Achaia, and there “he greatly helped those who through grace had become believers.” Paul will later sum up the partnership: “I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth” (1 Corinthians 3:6). No one owns the Gospel; each hands on what was received.

In the Gospel Jesus, at the Last Supper, speaks of a new way of praying: “if you ask anything of the Father in my name, he will give it to you … Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.” To ask in his name is not to add a formula at the end of a prayer; it is to pray as one who belongs to him, wanting what he wants. And then the most tender sentence: “the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.” We do not need Jesus to persuade an unwilling Father; the Father already loves us. Jesus sums up his whole life in one line: “I came from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and am going to the Father.” That is the movement the Church celebrates tomorrow in India, the Ascension. On this Saturday, a day dedicated to Our Lady, we remember that the apostles waited for the Spirit with Mary, the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14). She, who asked so simply at Cana, teaches us to ask in his name.
conn: Regions of central Asia Minor (modern Turkey) where Paul had founded churches on his earlier journeys (Acts 16:6). The Letter to the Galatians was written to churches in this area.
A great port city on the west coast of Asia Minor, with the famous temple of Artemis. Paul will soon stay there more than two years (Acts 19:10).

An Alexandrian Jew; Alexandria had a large Jewish community and was the city where the Greek translation of the Scriptures, the Septuagint, was made. Apollos later became so popular in Corinth that some said “I belong to Apollos” (1 Corinthians 1:12).
One of the earliest names for the Christian faith in Acts (9:2; 19:9; 24:14): not only a doctrine but a way of life following Jesus.
A baptism of repentance in preparation for the Messiah. Apollos knew Jesus, but not yet the full gift of Christian Baptism in the Holy Spirit (see Acts 19:1–7, read on Monday).
Early Christian communities welcomed travelling teachers with such letters (2 Corinthians 3:1; Romans 16:1). They were a sign of communion between churches.
In the Bible a name stands for the person. To ask in Jesus' name is to come before the Father as members of his Son, through him and with him.

From early times Saturday has been dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary; at Fatima (1917, and to Lucia in 1925) Our Lady also asked for the Communion of reparation on the first Saturday of five consecutive months, in honour of her Immaculate Heart.
altar: At every Mass the Church prays “through Christ our Lord”: every prayer is offered to the Father in the name of the Son. Above all in the Eucharistic Prayer, “through him, and with him, and in him,” our whole life is lifted to the Father.
Apollos was taught the Way more accurately. In the Mass we are taught first by the Word and then fed by the Bread; the table of the Word and the table of the Eucharist form one act of worship.
outline: Ask: when did someone take you aside and correct you kindly? How did it feel?
Priscilla, Aquila and the humble scholar.
Point 3 · The Father himself loves you
Mary in the upper room, hands open in prayer, the apostles around her.
live: Visit, phone or message one person whose faith is weak or tired, simply to encourage them.
If you must correct someone today, do it as Priscilla and Aquila did: privately, gently, with the aim of helping.
Bring one need to the Father today, beginning: Father, in the name of Jesus your Son, and ending with: your will be done.
fathers: Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ. Apollos was mighty in the Scriptures, and so he could show from them that Jesus is the Messiah.
See how Apollos, eloquent and learned, was not ashamed to be taught by a tentmaker and his wife. He learned, and so he was able to teach more powerfully.
Whatever we ask that is against our salvation we do not ask in the Saviour's name. To ask in the name of Jesus is to ask what belongs to our salvation, and that the Father gives.
magis: When Jesus openly entrusts to his disciples the mystery of prayer to the Father, he reveals to them what their prayer and ours must be: asking in his name.
The name of Jesus contains all: God and man and the whole economy of creation and salvation. To pray “Jesus” is to invoke him and to call him within us.
All the faithful are urged to learn by frequent reading of the Scriptures “the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus,” for ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.
After her Son's Ascension, Mary aided the beginnings of the Church by her prayers; with the apostles she implored the gift of the Spirit.
Women and men together share in the mission of the Church; the gifts of women are needed for the life and growth of the Christian community.
saints: The Supplication to Our Lady of Pompeii

On 8 May (and on the first Sunday of October) many Catholics recite at noon the Supplication to Our Lady of the Rosary of Pompeii, composed by Bartolo Longo, a lawyer who returned to the faith and built the shrine at Pompeii. He was canonized in October 2025.

9 May: THE ASCENSION OF THE LORD (in India); World Communications Day. 10 May: St John of Avila (optional). 11 May: Easter weekday. 12 May: Sts Nereus and Achilleus; St Pancras (optional). 13 May: Our Lady of Fatima (optional).
2027-05-08.prayer: Father, you love us because we have loved your Son and believed that he came from you. In his name we come to you, trusting that you hear us, and we ask above all for the gift of your Holy Spirit. Make us like Paul, strengthening the disciples; like Priscilla and Aquila, teaching the Way gently and truly; like Apollos, burning with zeal and humble enough to learn. With Mary, who prayed with the apostles while they waited, we wait for the Spirit and for the joy you promised to make complete. As your Son goes to you, let our hearts follow him. Through Christ our Lord. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: Paul set out again through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
In Ephesus, Priscilla and Aquila took the eloquent Apollos aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately.
Jesus: ask the Father in my name and you will receive; the Father himself loves you.
2027-05-08.action: Encourage one person whose faith is tired, by a visit, a call or a short message.
2027-05-08.question: Do I pray to the Father as someone who knows that he loves me?
catechism: Asking in the name of Jesus.
Mary at prayer with the infant Church.
kidsaint: Aquila and Priscilla were a husband and wife who made tents. They let St Paul live with them, worked with him, and opened their home for Christians to pray. When a clever preacher called Apollos did not know everything about Jesus, they invited him home and taught him kindly. Lesson: families can be missionaries too, and we can help others gently, without making them feel small.
2027-05-08.special: Easter weekday; Saturday in honour of Our Lady. In India, this evening's Mass is the Vigil Mass of the Ascension. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: To ask “in the name of Jesus” is to pray as his disciple, united with him, trusting in his authority and seeking his will. The liturgy ends its prayers “through Christ our Lord” for this reason.

family.explain: Jesus told his friends: ask the Father in my name, and he will give it to you. And then he said something beautiful: the Father himself loves you. God is not a stranger we must convince. He is a Father who already loves us, more than any parent loves a child.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who finds it hard to believe that God loves them, and for Christian families who open their homes to others.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we want to ask our Father for today?” Pray together, each beginning: Father, in the name of Jesus...

illus: In a parish in Kollam a young seminarian on his summer break was asked to preach at a weekday Mass. He spoke with great fire but said something about confession that was not quite right. After Mass an elderly couple, both retired teachers, invited him home for tea. Over banana fritters they gently opened the Catechism with him and showed him what the Church teaches. He was embarrassed for a moment, then grateful. Years later, as a parish priest, he told the story at their golden jubilee: they did not shame me from the pew; they corrected me at their table. That is how I learned to correct others.

pm.open: Father, in the name of Jesus we come to you, knowing that you love us. Send us your Holy Spirit. Alleluia. Amen.
share: He went from place to place, strengthening all the disciples (Acts 18:23). Whom can I strengthen this week?
They took him aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately (Acts 18:26). How do I correct others, and how do I accept correction?
The Father himself loves you (John 16:27). Do I really believe this, and how does it change my prayer?
pm.resp: God is king of all the earth.
interc: For missionaries and catechists who strengthen young churches.
For Christian couples who serve the Church together, and for all who open their homes to prayer and hospitality.
For preachers and teachers of the faith, that they may be both zealous and humble.
For those who find it hard to believe that God loves them.
For our group, waiting for the Holy Spirit with Mary, the Mother of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, your Son goes to you and you love us in him. Hear the prayers we make in his name and fill us with his joy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we meet a brilliant young preacher, Apollos from Alexandria. He was eloquent, he knew the Scriptures well, and he spoke about Jesus with burning enthusiasm. But there was something missing: he knew only the baptism of John.

Who noticed? Not a bishop, not an apostle, but a tentmaking couple, Priscilla and Aquila. And what did they do? They did not stand up in the synagogue and shout: you are wrong! They took him aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately (Acts 18:26). Probably at their own table, in their own home.

This is how Christians correct one another: privately, kindly, with the wish to help, not to win. And see the humility of Apollos: a learned man from the great city of Alexandria, he accepted teaching from two workers. Because he was humble, he became an even greater blessing to the Church.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches us to pray in his name: if you ask anything of the Father in my name, he will give it to you (John 16:23). And then he says: the Father himself loves you (John 16:27). Many of us pray as if God were an angry officer who must be persuaded. Jesus says no. The Father already loves you.

Jesus also says: I came from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and am going to the Father. Tomorrow, in India, we celebrate that return to the Father, the Ascension of the Lord.

Today is Saturday, a day dedicated to Mary. After the Ascension the apostles waited for the Holy Spirit, praying with Mary the mother of Jesus. Let us do the same: ask the Father, in Jesus' name, with Mary beside us, for the Holy Spirit. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, a clever preacher named Apollos did not know everything about Jesus. So Aquila and Priscilla invited him home and taught him kindly. We can help our friends kindly too!
Jesus says: the Father loves you! When you pray, you are talking to someone who loves you very much. Say: Father, I love you too!

intro: A missionary who goes back to strengthen, a couple who correct with love, and the Son who teaches us to ask in his name as he returns to the Father.

q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
After spending some time there he departed and went from place to place through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
points.apply: This week visit or call one person whose faith has grown weak, only to encourage them.

sub: Apollos: a gift, a fire and a gap.
Correction at the table, not from the pew.
q: Give instruction to the wise, and they will become wiser still; teach the righteous and they will gain in learning.
He began to speak boldly in the synagogue; but when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately.
points.apply: If you must correct someone this week, do it privately and kindly; and when you are corrected, say thank you.

sub: From the Father, to the Father.
q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.
For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
points.apply: Begin your prayers this week with the words: Father, you love me; in the name of Jesus I ask...

concl: Paul strengthened the disciples, Priscilla and Aquila taught Apollos with love, and Apollos humbly learned: the Gospel is handed on in a chain of humble service.
Jesus, returning to the Father, teaches us to pray in his name to a Father who already loves us; with Mary we ask for the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-08.resolve: Encourage one tired believer this week, and pray every day: Father, in Jesus' name, send us your Spirit.
